text.text_excerpt: We really liked our Tableau experience on a Friday night with a table for two. We dined at about 8:00 in the beautiful courtyard. The stand-out item of the evening was the crystal shrimp, an appetizer with a killer sauce. Our entrees were also good, and combined with the location in the heart of the French Quarter, I would definitely return. My one complaint was the service, which wasn't stellar, but we overlooked our servers' lack of attentiveness and enjoyed the evening. Worth a visit for the food and ambiance.

I honestly avoided restaurants smack in the center of the French Quarter because I assumed they would be overpriced for the quality. Tableau really changed my mind! Still on the pricier side, but not outrageous, but the food was incredible. For food, we got oysters for apps, steaks for entrees, and gulf fish. I personally like my dishes on the saltier side so some people may find the potato gratin with the steak slightly salty, but it complimented my medium rare steak perfectly. Ambiance ranges based on the room you're in. The main room downstairs is large, more traditional, and for larger tables. Upstairs there's a bar/lounge area that seems traditional but more laid back. I really enjoyed this place. The waitstaff were friendly and helpful and the food is excellent. I was here with a large party so was able to try several different dishes. - Grand Royale - We tried a variety of the appetizers which were oh so good. The truffled crab fingers are addictive. The oysters en brochette are amazing. Who could deny bacon wrapped oysters!? Seriously!? - Fried eggplant batons - Crispy and sweet at the same time. Very nice. - Filet of beef bearnaise - This was a good steak, but didn't knock my socks off. Perhaps in retrospect I should have gone with something more Creole instead of a filet.
